negotiation.solver_rationale: No discount offered: 13 days remain in the counterparty's 45-day MSME window, so settling early is already in their interest under Section 43B(h). Leverage, not margin.
negotiation.message: Invoice for Rs 340,000 is outstanding. 13 days remain in the 45-day MSME payment window; settling within it keeps this expense deductible for you in the current financial year under Section 43B(h).

negotiation.scenario: Window breached, economics justify a discount
negotiation.solver_rationale: 4.00% early-payment discount. Breakeven at 5.30% for a 120-day delay at 18% cost of capital; envelope caps at 4%.
negotiation.message: Invoice for Rs 180,000 is outstanding. The 45-day MSME window closed 35 days ago, so under Section 43B(h) this deduction now moves to the year of actual payment. We can offer a 4.0% early-payment discount if settled now.

negotiation.solver_rationale: Rs 900,000 exceeds the Rs 500,000 autonomy limit; a human must handle this negotiation.

ope.framing: single targeting decision per case (contact vs wait) at attempt 0, evaluated as a contextual bandit; not full-sequence OPE of the multi-step agent loop

fairness.scatter_note: a random sample of the evaluation batch; tau_hat is the model's predicted uplift, tau_true the simulator's hidden persuadability, amount the rupees at risk, contacted the decision the policy actually took

verdict.ranking_claim: top decile realises more uplift than bottom decile in every draw

revenue.outcome: spend — real dollars, two weeks post-treatment

effect.rule: Incremental revenue is claimable if its bootstrap interval excludes zero. Spend is heavy-tailed (0.9% of customers purchase; max $499), so a wide interval is expected and one covering zero is reported as covering zero.

effect_pooled_all_arms.note: effect of ANY email — a mixture of two campaigns, so a different estimand from the womens-only figure above

targeting_power.conclusion: Not a question this dataset can answer. The difference sits 0.44 standard errors from zero and resolving it needs roughly 20x the sample — about 420,871 held-out customers against the 32,000 pooling can supply. The targeting claim is not merely unproven here; it is unprovable on 64,000 customers at this effect size.

targeting.rule: Targeting is claimable only if the targeted policy's estimated value exceeds matched-volume random targeting AND IPS, SNIPS and DR agree on the sign of that difference. Disagreement in sign is published as UNDETERMINED.
targeting.registered_rule_was_weaker_than_the_ques: The rule asks only for sign agreement across three estimators computed from the same rows, which they will usually give whether or not the difference is real. The paired interval on the difference is the statistic that decides it, and it is reported here rather than substituted for the registered rule.
targeting.verdict: NOT ESTABLISHED: the three estimators agree on the sign, which is all the registered rule asked for, but the paired interval on the difference covers zero — the targeting advantage is not distinguishable from noise at this sample size.

targeting.note: binary outcome, not money — this tests the POLICY claim, not an effect size
targeting.rule: Targeting is claimable only if the paired bootstrap interval on (targeted minus matched-volume random) excludes zero AND all three estimators agree on the sign. Sign agreement alone was Tier 1b's rule and proved too weak; the bar is raised here before seeing any result.
targeting.verdict: CLAIMABLE: targeting beats matched-volume random targeting on real randomised data. The paired interval excludes zero and all three estimators agree on the sign. B1's central claim is no longer simulator-only.

recalibration.rule: Recalibration is claimable only if it increases incremental recovery and every draw agrees on the sign. A mean improvement across draws that disagree in sign is UNDETERMINED. The slope moving toward 1.0 is not the result — the correction is fitted to do that — the money is.

slope_on_heldout_population.note: the correction was fitted to move this; it is not the result

recalibration.verdict: UNDETERMINED: the draws disagree on the sign, so no effect on recovered value is established. The correction is not shipped on this evidence.

fleet_latency.claim_rule: Latency is claimable only if it replicates: the median latency must be finite and the detector must fire in every draw at the largest effect size. If the detector misses the change-point in any draw at that size, report the miss rate rather than a latency. A latency figure is only meaningful alongside the false-alarm rate measured on no-change control runs, so both are reported together or neither is claimed.
fleet_latency.verdict: CLAIMABLE: the detector fired in all 8 draws at the largest effect size swept (median latency 50 attempts), reported alongside a false-alarm rate of 0.0% measured on no-change control runs under the same polling procedure.

claims.statement: Do-not-disturbs opt out more than everyone else when contacted, so churn risk is a signal independent of predicted uplift.
claims.note: The supporting signal for N2. Published at 1.29x after the original 1.93x was found to be a single small-sample draw.

claims.statement: The uplift model's top decile realises more uplift than its bottom decile, in every draw.
Decile uplift is monotone: Spearman >= 0.9 in every draw.
claims.note: Fails at 0.879 on one draw. Reported as failed rather than rounded up; near-monotone is tracked as the weaker claim.

claims.statement: The model-judgement bucket contains a non-trivial count of refusals of customers who would have paid, as the calibration result requires.
The counterfactual's cost-side disagreement with the model-based estimate is a replicated finding.
claims.observed: UNRESOLVED: the realised cost fell outside the model-based cost interval in 3 of 6 draws (including the headline). The cost-side disagreement is NOT established as a replicated finding -- it is a property of which draw is examined, not of the method -- and must be reported as unresolved rather than as either a confirmed finding or a resolved non-finding.
claims.note: Outside the interval in 3 of 6 draws. Unresolved, and published as unresolved — the limitation itself did not replicate.

claims.statement: DR's low reading on Criteo is caused by cross-fitting starving the 15% minority arm, so more folds should shrink the gap.
claims.note: Refuted: coverage and mean gap are flat across a 10x fold range.

claims.statement: Detection latency is claimable: the detector fires in every draw at the largest effect size, reported with its false-alarm rate.
Contact produces incremental revenue, measured on a real randomised experiment with real dollars rather than in the simulator.
claims.note: The only money figure in this repo not produced by its own generator: $424 per 1,000 customers, interval excluding zero.

claims.statement: Targeting beats matched-volume random targeting on real money, not only in simulation.
claims.note: Not established. Three estimators agree on the sign - all the registered rule asked for - but the paired interval on the difference covers zero. The rule was weaker than the question and is left as registered, with the interval reported beside it.

claims.statement: Targeting beats contacting the same number of people at random, on real randomised data rather than in simulation.
claims.note: Held on Criteo under a rule deliberately stricter than Tier 1b's: the paired interval must exclude zero, not merely have three estimators agree on a sign. 8.94 SEs from zero.

claims.statement: Correcting tau_hat's measured over-spread increases incremental recovery.
claims.observed: UNDETERMINED: the draws disagree on the sign, so no effect on recovered value is established. The correction is not shipped on this evidence.
claims.note: Undetermined: the draws disagree on sign. The correction demonstrably works as arithmetic - the held-out slope moves 0.6674 to 0.9508 - and recovered value still does not follow consistently. Improving a diagnostic is not improving the decision.
The project's worst near-miss. Published as dominance from a run that no longer reproduced; it trades, it does not dominate.

prediction.rule: make calibration reports the bottom tau_hat bin as 43.8% true do-not-disturbs, so it is also ~56% customers with positive true uplift. The model-judgement bucket must therefore contain a non-trivial count of tau_true > 0 refusals. Near zero refutes one of the two experiments.

counterfactual_check.one_sided_because: the universe excludes resolved cases, so paid_0 is ~0 by selection and a realised saving cannot be observed

disagreement_replication.rule: The cost-side disagreement is a replicated finding only if the realised cost falls outside the model-based interval in every draw. If it falls outside in some draws and inside in others, the disagreement is not established and must be reported as unresolved -- a property of the headline draw rather than of the method. If it falls inside in every draw, the headline draw was the outlier and that must be published as such. Either conclusion requires at least 3 draws; below that floor, report that too few draws were run to conclude anything, not a replicated finding or a resolved non-finding.
disagreement_replication.verdict: UNRESOLVED: the realised cost fell outside the model-based cost interval in 3 of 6 draws (including the headline). The cost-side disagreement is NOT established as a replicated finding -- it is a property of which draw is examined, not of the method -- and must be reported as unresolved rather than as either a confirmed finding or a resolved non-finding.

RBI.RECOVERY.HOURS.instrument: RBI — Outsourcing of Financial Services: Responsibilities of regulated entities employing Recovery Agents
RBI.RECOVERY.HOURS.requirement: Regulated entities must ensure their recovery agents do not contact borrowers before 8:00 a.m. or after 7:00 p.m.
RBI.RECOVERY.HOURS.encoded_as: Customer-facing actions are denied outside 08:00–19:00 IST. RETRY and WAIT are exempt — a silent retry is not contact.
RBI.RECOVERY.HOURS.note: The window is the circular's. The RETRY/WAIT exemption is our reading: the prohibition is on contacting the borrower, and a background retry does not reach them.

RBI.RECOVERY.TONE_CEILING.instrument: RBI — Outsourcing of Financial Services: Responsibilities of regulated entities employing Recovery Agents
RBI.RECOVERY.TONE_CEILING.requirement: Recovery agents must not resort to intimidation or harassment, verbal or physical, in the recovery process.
RBI.RECOVERY.TONE_CEILING.encoded_as: Message tone intensity (0 neutral … 3 firm) is capped by genuine attempt history: ≤1 on the first contact, ≤2 on the second, ≤3 thereafter. An escalation ladder cannot open at its top rung.
RBI.RECOVERY.TONE_CEILING.note: The prohibition is the circular's; the 0–3 intensity scale is this project's invention. No regulator publishes a numeric tone scale — this is a machine-checkable proxy for it, not a restatement of law.

TCCCPR.DLT.REGISTERED.instrument: TRAI Telecom Commercial Communications Customer Preference Regulations, 2018
TCCCPR.DLT.REGISTERED.requirement: Commercial communication may be sent only by senders registered on the distributed-ledger (DLT) platform, using registered headers and registered content templates.
TCCCPR.DLT.REGISTERED.encoded_as: An unregistered sender or template denies the action.

TCCCPR.HEADER.CLASS_MATCH.instrument: TRAI Telecom Commercial Communications Customer Preference Regulations, 2018
TCCCPR.HEADER.CLASS_MATCH.requirement: Headers are registered against a communication category, and a header may not be used to send a different category of message.
TCCCPR.HEADER.CLASS_MATCH.encoded_as: The template's registered class (-P/-S/-T/-G) must equal the message's declared class. Promotional content on a service header is denied.

TCCCPR.CONSENT.VALIDITY.instrument: TRAI Telecom Commercial Communications Customer Preference Regulations, 2018
TCCCPR.CONSENT.VALIDITY.requirement: Commercial communication requires a valid basis — explicit consent, or an inferred basis arising from an existing relationship — and that basis can lapse.
TCCCPR.CONSENT.VALIDITY.encoded_as: Inferred consent lapses when the underlying contract is no longer active; explicit consent for service-class messages expires 7 days after capture.
TCCCPR.CONSENT.VALIDITY.note: The 7-day expiry is the least certain rule in the kernel. COMPLIANCE.md records the ambiguity rather than resolving it silently: the project chose the stricter reading, which can only cost recovery, never compliance.

TCCCPR.OPT_OUT.OPTION_PRESENT.instrument: TRAI Telecom Commercial Communications Customer Preference Regulations, 2018
TCCCPR.OPT_OUT.OPTION_PRESENT.requirement: Promotional communication must carry a means for the recipient to opt out.
TCCCPR.OPT_OUT.OPTION_PRESENT.encoded_as: Promotional-class messages without an opt-out affordance are denied. Service and transactional classes are exempt from this specific check.

TCCCPR.OPT_OUT.COOLING.instrument: TRAI Telecom Commercial Communications Customer Preference Regulations, 2018
TCCCPR.OPT_OUT.COOLING.requirement: A recipient's revocation of consent must be honoured, and a sender may not immediately re-solicit consent after it.
TCCCPR.OPT_OUT.COOLING.encoded_as: After an opt-out, no further contact and no consent request for 90 days unless the customer opts back in.

TCCCPR.NUMBER_SERIES.instrument: TRAI Telecom Commercial Communications Customer Preference Regulations, 2018
TCCCPR.NUMBER_SERIES.requirement: Commercial calling and messaging must originate from the numbering series allocated for that category — the 140 series for promotional traffic, the 160 series for transactional and service traffic.
TCCCPR.NUMBER_SERIES.encoded_as: The sender's number series must match the declared message class.
TCCCPR.NUMBER_SERIES.note: Series allocation has been directed by TRAI across several instruments rather than one clause; the project models it as a single series-to-class check.

EMANDATE2026.PRE_DEBIT_NOTICE.instrument: RBI framework for e-mandates on recurring transactions
EMANDATE2026.PRE_DEBIT_NOTICE.requirement: The issuer must send the customer a pre-debit notification at least 24 hours before a recurring mandate is charged, carrying the transaction details and a way to opt out.
EMANDATE2026.PRE_DEBIT_NOTICE.encoded_as: A debit attempt (modelled as RETRY against a mandate-backed case) is denied unless a pre-debit notice was sent ≥24 hours earlier.
EMANDATE2026.PRE_DEBIT_NOTICE.note: The rule id names the buildathon spec's forward-dated 'E-Mandate Framework, 2026'. The 24-hour pre-debit notification it describes is the same requirement RBI's existing e-mandate framework for recurring transactions already imposes, which is why the rule is encoded against a real obligation rather than a hypothetical one. AFA requirements for mandate registration and modification are deliberately not encoded — no ActionType in this project can register or modify a mandate, so the rule would be vacuous.

DPDPA.CONSENT_RECORD.requirement: Personal data may be processed only for a lawful purpose for which the data principal has given consent, preceded by notice.
DPDPA.CONSENT_RECORD.encoded_as: Customer contact requires an on-record consent capture timestamp. The rule checks that a record exists, not that the consent is still current — TCCCPR.CONSENT.VALIDITY does that.
DPDPA.CONSENT_RECORD.note: Purpose limitation and retention are not encoded as per-action rules. They are properties of what the system stores, not predicates about one candidate action; COMPLIANCE.md records retention as an open gap rather than faking a rule for it.

POLICY.CONTACT_BUDGET.requirement: Internal limit. No regulator sets this number; the project sets it so an agent cannot pursue one customer indefinitely.
POLICY.CONTACT_BUDGET.encoded_as: At most 3 contact attempts per rolling 7-day window per case.
POLICY.CONTACT_BUDGET.note: Policy, not law. Tightening it costs recovery and breaks nothing.

POLICY.PROMISE_TO_PAY_WINDOW.requirement: Internal limit, adopted because chasing a customer who has already committed to a date is the harassment pattern the RBI norms exist to prevent, even where no single message breaches them.
POLICY.PROMISE_TO_PAY_WINDOW.encoded_as: Once a customer promises a payment date, contact is denied until that date plus a two-day grace period.
POLICY.PROMISE_TO_PAY_WINDOW.note: Policy, not law — but the reason for it is the law's reason.

POLICY.NEGOTIATION_ENVELOPE.requirement: Internal limit. The agent may not concede more than the envelope the operator authorised, and may not offer a discount that destroys more value than the delay it avoids.
POLICY.NEGOTIATION_ENVELOPE.encoded_as: A settlement offer is denied if it exceeds the authorised discount ceiling or the case's autonomy limit in rupees.
POLICY.NEGOTIATION_ENVELOPE.note: The envelope is sized against Section 43B(h) of the Income-tax Act, 1961 (inserted by the Finance Act, 2023) read with s. 15 of the MSMED Act, 2006: a buyer who does not pay a micro or small enterprise within the statutory window has the deduction deferred to the year of actual payment, which is what makes early settlement the buyer's own interest. That statute shapes the negotiation; it does not impose this rule.
